system_prompt_style.note: System prompt assembled from per-agent config description plus tool-list plan instruction.

env_context_strategy.note: Simulated tool environment; no repository/file-system context is injected beyond task text and tool descriptions.

context_compaction.note: Messages are appended without any truncation or summarization in the run loop.

observation_format.evidence_quote: observations.append(f"The knowledge I get from {function_name} is: {function_response}")

tool_call_format.note: OpenAI-style function schemas; plan is emitted as JSON in text.

tool_count.note: Over 400 attack tools additionally available; each agent exposes its own subset from its config tools list.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote:
def run(self, params=None) -> str:

edit_primitive.note: Tools are simulated and return canned strings; no file editing primitive.

tool_schema_source.note: Schemas built from hand-authored JSONL tool descriptions.

protocol_standardization.note: Tools loaded by local module import / JSONL file; no MCP or A2A client in evidence.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: 'Generate a plan of steps you need to take.'
loop_primitives.note: ReactAgent generates a workflow plan then executes each step.

planning_granularity.note: Plan is a validated JSON list of {message, tool_use} steps iterated by run().

multi_agent_topology.note: One agent per task; 10 scenario agents run independently.

human_in_loop.note: Tool calls executed directly with no approval gate.

short_term_state.note: Workflow plan object is also held, but state is essentially the message list.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: the agent saves the task execution history to the memory database after a task operation
long_term_memory.note: RAG memory database of query-plan pairs retrieved as in-context examples; read_db/write_db configurable.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: read_db: whether to read the database.
state_persistence.note: DB read/write is memory, not run resumption; no resume path in evidence.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Leverage the LLM to identify compromised memory.
self_verification.note: LLM-based detection and PPL detection are config-selectable defenses; not verification of agent work quality.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: self.plan_max_fail_times = 3 # 这个变量表示在生成计划时，允许计划失败的最大次数
retry_policy.note: Plan regeneration up to 3 times; tool_call_max_fail_times = 3.

rollback.evidence_quote:
def run(self, params=None) -> str:

rollback.note: Simulated tools make no persistent changes, so no rollback exists.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: for i, step in enumerate(workflow): # 处理工作流程中的每一步
termination_condition.note: Run ends when the generated plan's steps are exhausted.

cost_controls.note: Only timing statistics collected; no budget, routing or cache in evidence.

timeouts.note: Only an internal queue poll timeout; no tool or run timeout.

execution_isolation.note: Tools are simulated in-process; nothing is actually executed externally.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote:
def run(self, params=None) -> str:

filesystem_access.note: No real filesystem access; tool effects are simulated strings.

network_policy.evidence_quote: llms: The LLMs to use in the evaluation. Please add "ollama/" for open-source LLMs.
network_policy.note: No network restriction configuration; LLM API/ollama calls go out freely.

permission_model.note: Any model-selected tool is executed; prompt-level defenses are the only controls.

tracing.note: Logs saved under logs/ with a run suffix.

replayability.evidence_quote: suffix: To distinguish between different runs, append a unique identifier to the end of the log file name (in logs/).
replayability.note: Logs only; no replay path in evidence.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: python scripts/agent_attack.py --cfg_path config/DPI.yml # Direct Prompt Injection
eval_hooks.note: ASB is itself the benchmark runner with ASR/RR/PNA/NRP metrics.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Use delimiters to encapsulate the user query, ensuring that the agent solely executes the user query within the delimiters.
guardrails.note: Defenses are config-selectable (delimiters, paraphrasing, instructional prevention on inputs; sandwich/PPL/LLM detection on tool responses and memory); default is no defense.
